disposition_reason: Table 3 prints wet-weight cadmium, lead, nickel, arsenic and mercury in mealworm larvae reared on five feeding substrates.

study.design: rearing experiment: five feeding substrates (wheat flour, wheatmeal, wheatmeal with 25/50/75% olive pomace), 3 replicates of 4000 larvae each
study.origin: colony started from larvae bought at a pet shop in Ancona, Italy; reared in a climatic chamber
study.method: microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion; GF-AAS (Agilent 240FS, Zeeman) for Cd, Pb, Ni, As, Se; direct mercury analyzer (DMA-1) for Hg; ISO class 6 clean room
study.lod_text: not stated; procedural blanks <1% of sample concentrations
study.qa: DORM-2 dogfish muscle CRM: Cd +2%, Pb +6%, Ni -11%, As -5.5%, Hg +3%, Se -1% vs certified

controls.comparator: 100% organic wheatmeal vs wheat flour and olive-pomace blends
controls.outcome: Larval Ni rose from 0.030 (wheat flour) / 0.26 (wheatmeal) to 0.63 mg/kg ww at 75% olive pomace; Hg rose 0.12e-3 -> 0.49e-3 mg/kg ww; Pb 0.063-0.079, Cd 0.008-0.016 and As 0.021-0.023 mg/kg ww changed little

Pb BAF 34 (wheat flour), 5.2 (wheatmeal), 6.1 / 9.8 / 12 (25/50/75% pomace); Hg BAF 1.5-6.2; Cd 0.8-1.9; As 0.53-1.07; Ni 0.17-1.18. Authors suggest carrots given as water source may explain high larval Pb (not verified)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU food limits used for comparison (Reg. 1881/2006, 420/2011, 1006/2015)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Cd 0.05 (meat), Pb 0.1 (meat), As 0.20 (rice, inorganic), Hg 0.5 (fish) mg/kg ww

unresolved: Dry-weight larval concentrations per diet are figure-only (Figs 1-5); text gives dw ranges only (e.g. Cd 28-46, Pb 190-290 µg/kg dw).
Substrate and frass values are feed/excreta, not findings.
Se values not printed in a table (figure-only).
